sentences.en: We get support from UC Davis, a globally ranked university working to solve the world's most pressing problems in food, energy, health, education, and the environment.
sentences.zh: 我们得到加州大学戴维斯分校的支持，这是一所全球知名的大学，致力于解决世界在食品、能源、健康、教育和环境方面最紧迫的问题。

sentences.en: UC Davis researchers collaborate and innovate in California and around the globe to find transformational solutions.
sentences.zh: 加州大学戴维斯分校的研究人员在加州乃至全球范围内合作创新，以寻找变革性的解决方案。

sentences.en: It's all part of the university's mission to promote quality of life for all living things.
sentences.zh: 这一切都是该大学旨在提升所有生物生活质量的使命的一部分。

sentences.en: Find out more at 21stCentury.UCDavis.edu.
sentences.zh: 请访问 21stCentury.UCDavis.edu 了解更多信息。

sentences.en: This is 99% Invisible.
sentences.zh: 这里是《99%无形》。

sentences.en: I'm Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 我是罗曼·马尔斯。

sentences.en: This is the first joke I ever really noticed as a design joke.
sentences.zh: 这是我真正注意到的第一个被当成设计的笑话。

sentences.en: I like an escalator, man, because an escalator can never break.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢自动扶梯，伙计，因为自动扶梯永远不会坏。

sentences.en: It can only become stairs.
sentences.zh: 它只会变成楼梯。

sentences.en: That's Mitch Hedberg.
sentences.zh: 那是米奇·赫德伯格说的。

sentences.en: There would never be an escalator temporarily out of order sign.
sentences.zh: 绝对不会有显示“自动扶梯暂停使用”的标牌。

sentences.en: Only an escalator temporarily stairs.
sentences.zh: 只会是“自动扶梯临时变成楼梯”。

sentences.en: Sorry for the convenience.
sentences.zh: 抱歉给您带来了便利。

sentences.en: Being designed to elegantly deal with the extreme failure case is probably an underappreciated design element.
sentences.zh: 被设计来优雅地应对极端故障情况，可能是一个被低估的设计元素。

sentences.en: But it really is one of the things that makes an escalator great.
sentences.zh: 但它确实是让自动扶梯如此出色的原因之一。

sentences.en: Worst case, there's stairs.
sentences.zh: 最坏的情况，还有楼梯。

sentences.en: See how far you get in a broken elevator.
sentences.zh: 看看你在坏掉的电梯里能走多远。

sentences.en: I bet everyone on this escalator is enjoying that design aspect too.
sentences.zh: 我敢说这扶梯上的每个人也很享受这种设计层面。

sentences.en: And we're getting our cardio.
sentences.zh: 而且我们还在进行有氧运动。

sentences.en: That's 99% Invisible Zone's Sam Green's fan walking up an escalator in a metro station in DC.
sentences.zh: 那是《99%无形》之城萨姆·格林的粉丝在华盛顿特区地铁站走扶梯的场景。

sentences.en: Ever since the industrial revolution when it became possible for products to be designed just once and then mass produced,
sentences.zh: 自从工业革命以来，产品可以被设计一次然后批量生产，

sentences.en: it has been the slight failures and imperfections and the individual wear and tear introduced by human use
sentences.zh: 正是人类使用过程中引入的微小故障、瑕疵以及个人的磨损，

sentences.en: that transforms a quality mass-produced product into a thing we actually love.
sentences.zh: 才将一个优质的量产产品变成我们真正喜爱的事物。

sentences.en: Your worn-in blue jeans.
sentences.zh: 你那穿旧的牛仔裤。

sentences.en: Your grandmother's iron skillet.
sentences.zh: 你祖母用的铁煎锅。

sentences.en: The initial design determined its quality.
sentences.zh: 最初的设计决定了它的品质。

sentences.en: But it's their post-manufacturing imperfections that make them comfortable,
sentences.zh: 但正是它们制造后的瑕疵让它们用起来舒适，

sentences.en: that make them lovable,
sentences.zh: 让它们讨人喜欢，

sentences.en: that make them yours.
sentences.zh: 让它们真正属于你。

sentences.en: And if you think a slightly broken escalator can't be lovable,
sentences.zh: 如果你认为稍微坏掉的扶梯不会讨人喜欢，

sentences.en: well, maybe you haven't been paying attention.
sentences.zh: 好吧，也许你一直没怎么关注。

sentences.en: An escalator on a DC metro platform is like a fine wine.
sentences.zh: 华盛顿地铁站台上的扶梯就像一款上好的葡萄酒。

sentences.en: It's better with age and without any industrial lubricant.
sentences.zh: 历经岁月的沉淀且不含任何工业润滑剂，它反而更美妙。

sentences.en: Sam lives in Baltimore now, but he lived in DC for a few years.
sentences.zh: 萨姆现在住在巴尔的摩，但他在华盛顿特区住过几年。

sentences.en: He said that this sound came to embody the excitement he felt from living in a city.
sentences.zh: 他说，这种声音开始具体化他居住在城市中所感受到的兴奋感。

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean, I grew up in one of Florida's most depressing suburbs.
sentences.zh: 对啊，我的意思是，我在佛罗里达最令人沮丧的郊区之一长大。

sentences.en: I mean, it's just miles and miles of highways and coals to sack.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，那里到处都是数不清的高速公路和死胡同。

sentences.en: Very nice.
sentences.zh: 非常好。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: So when I moved to DC, I took public transit everywhere just because I could.
sentences.zh: 所以当我搬到华盛顿特区时，我到处都坐公共交通，仅仅因为我可以。

sentences.en: The DC metro system, it's not the best in the world, but it's pretty good.
sentences.zh: 华盛顿地铁系统，虽然不是世界上最好的，但也算相当不错。

sentences.en: Although a lot of people do lament the poor condition of the metro's escalators.
sentences.zh: 尽管很多人确实在抱怨地铁扶梯糟糕的状况。

sentences.en: Some are just flat out broken, and then there are some that work but make these crazy noises,
sentences.zh: 有些直接彻底坏了，还有些还能运行但会发出这种疯狂的噪音，

sentences.en: which, you know, annoy a lot of people.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，这让很多人感到烦恼。

sentences.en: But for me, I found that a skronking escalator was like this little trumpeter
sentences.zh: 但对我来说，我发现一台发出刺耳声音的扶梯就像一个小号手，

sentences.en: announcing how awesome it was to live in the city.
sentences.zh: 宣告着住在城里是多么带劲。

sentences.en: It turns out that someone else loves this sound, too.
sentences.zh: 原来也有别人同样喜欢这个声音。

sentences.en: So this is Chris Richards.
sentences.zh: 这位是克里斯·理查兹。

sentences.en: I'm the pop music critic at the Washington PoSt.
sentences.zh: 我是《华盛顿邮报》的流行音乐评论员。

sentences.en: Chris was also in a band called Q and Not You.
sentences.zh: 克里斯曾在一个叫“Q和不是你”的乐队里。

sentences.en: He wrote a kind of appreciation of the metro escalators for the PoSt.
sentences.zh: 他为《华盛顿邮报》写了一篇类似赞赏地铁扶梯的文章。

sentences.en: We're at the Farragut North Metro Station in Washington, D.C.,
sentences.zh: 我们现在在华盛顿特区的法拉格特北地铁站，

sentences.en: on the north side of L Street and Connecticut Avenue.
sentences.zh: 位于L街和康涅狄格大道交汇处的北侧。

sentences.en: Chris told me that he had never really noticed the sound that the escalators made
sentences.zh: 克里斯告诉我，他以前从未真正注意到扶梯发出的声音，

sentences.en: until one day when he was on a bit of a free jazz kick.
sentences.zh: 直到有一天他正迷恋于自由爵士乐。

sentences.en: Having my ear trained for those sort of breath on brass kind of sounds,
sentences.zh: 由于我的耳朵已经习惯了那种铜管乐器里气流之类的声音，

sentences.en: I think maybe turning the corner to come down the escalators one day,
sentences.zh: 我想也许有一天转过拐角走下扶梯时，

sentences.en: I thought, oh, there's a saxophone player playing at the bottom of the metro.
sentences.zh: 我心想，哦，地铁底部有个萨克斯手在演奏呢。

sentences.en: But it wasn't that at all.
sentences.zh: 但根本不是那回事。

sentences.en: It's just the escalators kind of like wonking and screeching away.
sentences.zh: 那只是扶梯在发出一声声刺耳、尖锐的怪声。

sentences.en: Maybe they were, I don't know if they were always this loud.
sentences.zh: 也许它们本来就是这样，我不知道它们是不是一直都这么吵。

sentences.en: On the escalator, there's a plastic element on the side of each step
sentences.zh: 在扶梯上，每个台阶的侧面都有一个塑料部件，

sentences.en: that keeps it from rubbing against the metal siding.
sentences.zh: 可以防止它与金属侧板摩擦。

sentences.en: A lubricant keeps it all running smoothly.
sentences.zh: 润滑剂能让这一切顺畅运行。

sentences.en: But when it rains or snows, the lubrication wears off.
sentences.zh: 但当下雨或下雪时，润滑油就会磨损掉。

sentences.en: So what you're hearing when you hear these kind of like moaning squawks
sentences.zh: 所以当你听到这种类似呻吟和怪叫的声音时，

sentences.en: is the steel stairs sort of rubbing up and chafing against that plastic element
sentences.zh: 其实是钢制台阶在过度干燥的情况下，

sentences.en: when it's gotten a little too dry.
sentences.zh: 与那个塑料部件产生摩擦和擦伤。

sentences.en: Kind of like a beautiful, serendipitous aftershock of the wear and tear
sentences.zh: 这有点像这些扶梯所面临的磨损带来的美好而意外的余波。

sentences.en: that these escalators are facing.
sentences.zh: 听起来就像音乐一样。

sentences.en: It sounds like music.
sentences.zh: 就像任何优秀的乐评人一样，

sentences.en: And like any good music critic,
sentences.zh: 克里斯开始对不同风格的地铁扶梯进行分类。

sentences.en: Chris started classifying the different styles of metro escalator.
sentences.zh: 所以在法拉格特北站，这里的扶梯听起来可能像是……

sentences.en: So here at Fairgate North, the escalators might sound like...
sentences.zh: 鲸鱼交配，诸如此类的声音。

sentences.en: Whales mating, or something like that.
sentences.zh: 而U街站的扶梯……

sentences.en: Whereas the escalator at U Street...
sentences.zh: 听起来有点像印度的持续低音音乐。

sentences.en: Kind of sounded like Indian drone music.
sentences.zh: 至于哥伦比亚高地站……

sentences.en: And at Columbia Heights...
sentences.zh: 就像是一群镀喉渡鸦的鸟舍，在你走向工作岗位时对你冷嘲热讽。

sentences.en: An aviary of chrome-throated ravens taunting you as you descend into your workday.
sentences.zh: 我们明白，我们可能把一台刺耳尖叫的扶梯过度浪漫化了。

sentences.en: We understand that we could be over-romanticizing a skronking and squeaking escalator.
sentences.zh: 你可以一整天都在谈论欣赏身边的环境音景，

sentences.en: You can talk all day about appreciating the ambient soundscape around you
sentences.zh: 并且深深沉迷于审美化的聆听方式中。

sentences.en: and get really into aestheticized ways of listening.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，克里斯·理查兹就很热衷于此。

sentences.en: Chris Richards was big on this, by the way.
sentences.zh: 但你同样也可以轻而易举地说，嘿，这全都是噪音。

sentences.en: But you could also just as easily say, you know, hey, this is all noise.
sentences.zh: 我认为这完全取决于听众各自的感受。

sentences.en: I think it's all really in the ear of the beholder.
sentences.zh: 对，人们不欣赏刺耳的扶梯完全是可以理解的。

sentences.en: Yeah, it is totally understandable that people wouldn't appreciate a screeching escalator.
sentences.zh: 克里斯事实上告诉我，当他为自己的报道打电话给地铁公司时，

sentences.en: Chris actually told me that when he called up Metro for his story,
sentences.zh: 他们的公关人员根本不相信他。

sentences.en: their PR people didn't believe him.
sentences.zh: 他们以为他在写什么关于扶梯故障的重磅丑闻报道。

sentences.en: They thought he was writing some big expose about escalator failure.
sentences.zh: 事实恰恰相反。

sentences.en: Quite the opposite, really.
sentences.zh: 我想说的是，你知道的，尽管这些东西有点破旧，

sentences.en: I was trying to say, you know, even though these things are a little bit beat down,
sentences.zh: 我想这也是一个绝妙的小小附加福利。

sentences.en: this is a wonderful little residual bonus, I guess.
sentences.zh: 我的观点是，如果你每天都要被迫经历某种你无法控制的感官体验，

sentences.en: My point of view is if you're going to be subjected to some kind of sensory experience
sentences.zh: 那么这对你是有好处的。

sentences.en: of which you have no control every single day, then it's to your benefit.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，为什么不试着去享受点什么呢？

sentences.en: It's, you know, why not try to enjoy something?
sentences.zh: 因为生活中让人感到压力的事情已经够多了。

sentences.en: Because there's enough things in life to be stressed out about.
sentences.zh: 尽管人们总是抱怨城市里所有的声音

sentences.en: As much as people complain about all the sounds that cities make
sentences.zh: 和城市里所有的噪音，

sentences.en: and all the noises that cities make,
sentences.zh: 但我认为这些噪音定义了城市，并且，你知道的，真正成为了我们的环境。

sentences.en: I think those noises define it and, you know, really become our environment.
sentences.zh: 声音可以是一种干扰，也可以是信息。

sentences.en: The sound can be an irritation or it can be information.
sentences.zh: 克里斯让我希望这些扶梯永远不要修好。

sentences.en: Chris got me hoping the escalators never get fixed.
sentences.zh: 除了那些直接彻底罢工的。

sentences.en: Except the ones that just straight up don't work.
sentences.zh: 惠顿站的扶梯是西半球最长的扶梯。

sentences.en: The escalator at the Wheaton stop, it is the longest escalator in the Western Hemisphere.
sentences.zh: 正常运转时，坐到顶端需要三分钟。

sentences.en: It takes three minutes to ride to the top when it's working.
sentences.zh: 但愿惠顿扶梯不会在短期内“便利地”变成楼梯。

sentences.en: Let's hope that the Wheaton escalator doesn't conveniently become stairs anytime soon.

sentences.en: To find out more or keep in touch with us,

sentences.en: especially if you want to tell us about your favorite sound,
sentences.zh: 你知道的，那个你确信对别人来说只是噪音的声音——

sentences.en: which you know, which you know for a fact is somebody else's noise,
sentences.zh: 请访问我们的网站。

sentences.en: go to our website.
sentences.zh: 网址是 99percentinvisible.org。
